_overridesNote: brace-expansion carries TWO high-severity DoS advisories, and the second one inverted
which of our copies are at risk. Read both before touching this block.
GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg was patched within every major at 1.1.17 / 2.1.3 / 3.0.3 / 5.0.8.
GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 then BYPASSED that mitigation, and its range is
`2.0.0 - 2.1.3 || 4.0.0 - 5.0.8` -- 1.x is not in it at all. So the earlier version of
this note, which concluded that only the 1.x copies needed moving and that our 2.x and
5.x were already safe, now names exactly the wrong copies. The fix versions are 2.1.4
and 5.0.9. Both are same-major moves, so neither changes an export shape.
Everything still arrives through dev tooling -- eslint, electron-builder, ejs/jake --
so nothing that ships is affected. Current consumers: minimatch 3.x pins 1.x;
minimatch 9.x (via dir-compare) and minimatch 5.x (via filelist/jake/ejs) pin 2.x;
minimatch 10.x pins 5.x.
ONE SCOPED SELECTOR PER MAJOR. Never a bare `brace-expansion`. A bare override drags
every consumer to 5.x, which CHANGED ITS EXPORT SHAPE: 1.x/2.x are
`module.exports = expandTop`, 5.x is `module.exports = { expand, ... }`. minimatch 3.x
does `var expand = require('brace-expansion')` and calls it, so a bare override dies
with `TypeError: expand is not a function` -- but ONLY for a pattern containing braces,
because minimatch 3.x short-circuits braceExpand for patterns without them. Our eslint
config globs `**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,cjs}`, so we would hit it on the first lint; a config
with no braces passes and ships the landmine instead.
Scoping keeps each major on its own line: minimatch 3.x keeps a default-export 1.1.18,
the 2.x consumers keep a default-export 2.1.4, and minimatch 10.x keeps 5.0.9, whose
named `expand` it imports. No @eslint/config-array pin is needed, and each selector
simply stops matching when its last consumer goes -- nothing has to be removed by hand.
Verified: `npm audit` is clean, eslint still reports a SEEDED violation (proving the
glob did not silently start matching zero files), and minimatch 3.x still expands
`**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` correctly under 1.1.18.
